ov: Fast-swimming molluscs with large eyes, eight arms and two long tentacles. Many move by jet propulsion, hunt by sight, and can squirt ink to confuse predators.

why.et: Squid are caught for food by commercial fisheries in Japan, the Mediterranean, the Atlantic, the Pacific and elsewhere.

df: Fish and other open-water prey, grabbed with the two tentacles and held with the eight arms.

cf.tip: A squid has eight arms plus two long tentacles and a small internal “pen” for support. An octopus has eight arms and no tentacles.

fx: The giant squid’s eyes, at least 27 cm across, are the largest of any living animal except perhaps the colossal squid’s.
